AR.name: Arbol de las orquideas
AR.citation: Argentine gardening blog documenting active cultivation in Cordoba, Argentina: 'Aqui la conocemos como arbol de las orquideas por el parecido de sus flores'. SAFETY/COLLISION NOTE: the same source explicitly warns the plant's leaves resemble, and are often confused with, Argentina's own native tree also called 'pata de vaca' (northern Argentina) - a different species. 'Pata de vaca' is deliberately NOT used as the Argentina name here to avoid that collision; 'arbol de las orquideas' is the unambiguous term.

CO.name: Casco de vaca
CO.citation: Universidad EIA official flora catalog (Catalogo Flora Valle de Aburra, Colombia): 'Casco de vaca (variegata), arbol orquidea (Bauhinia variegata)'. SAFETY/COLLISION NOTE: Colombia also has a native, unrelated species (Bauhinia picta, native from Panama to Venezuela) sharing the same common names 'casco de vaca'/'arbol orquidea' - the academic catalog entry cited here explicitly labels this specific entry '(variegata)' to distinguish the introduced Asian species from the native look-alike.

IN.name: Kachnar
IN.citation: Standard Hindi name for this species' edible flower buds, widely documented (Wikipedia species article, multiple horticultural and Ayurvedic sources) as a genuine market/culinary item across North India, used in curries and pickles.

MX.name: Arbol Orquidea
MX.citation: Bio Campeche (official biodiversity portal of the Mexican state of Campeche): 'Nombre Cientifico: Bauhinia variegata L. Nombre Comun: Arbol Orquidea'. Independently corroborated by UNAM's (Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico) vascular plants catalog, which gives 'Arbol orquidea, Pata de vaca, Pata de res'.

US.name: Orchid-tree
US.citation: Flora of the Southeastern United States (FSUS, official regional flora database): 'Bauhinia variegata Linnaeus. Common name: Orchid-tree. Habitat: Disturbed areas.' Documented as naturalized in the southeastern US.
